## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical, real-world maintenance of TLS in a single-host stack with zero downtime, SELinux awareness, and validation.

- Zero-downtime certificate rotation
- Atomic symlink swap for ssl_certificate paths

## Code Example

# renewal (example use with certbot)
certbot renew --deploy-hook "cp /etc/ssl/app/cert.pem /etc/ssl/app/cert-new.pem; cp /etc/ssl/app/privkey.pem /etc/ssl/app/key-new.pem"

# swap and reload (atomic)

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical TLS forwarding, selective log routing, certificate handling, and zero-downtime reloads. It also assesses SELinux policy framing and firewall integration.

## Key Concepts
- rsyslog TLS forward with omfwd and per-facility selectors
- TLS certs in /etc/pki/rsyslog/certs and TLS parameters
- systemd drop-in for zero-downtime reload
- SELinux policy to permit cert access and network egress
- firewall-cmd port 6514/tcp and connectivity checks

## Code Example
```bash
# /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward-tls.conf
global(
  DefaultNetstreamDriver="gtls"
)
$DefaultNetstreamDriverCAFile /etc/pki/rsyslog/certs/ca.pem
$DefaultNetstreamDriverCertFile /etc/pki/rsyslog/certs/client.pem
$DefaultNetstreamDriverKeyFile /etc/pki/rsyslog/certs/client.key
kern.*;auth.*;mail.*  action(type="omfwd" Target="192.168.100.50" Port="6514" Protocol="tcp" TLS="on" TLSCAFile="/etc/pki/rsyslog/certs/ca.pem" TLSCert="/etc/pki/rsyslog/certs/client.pem" TLSKey="/etc/pki/rsyslog/certs/client.key" ReconnectDelay="20")
```

```bash
# /etc/systemd/system/rsyslog-forwarder.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
```

```bash
# rsyslog SELinux policy (te)
policy_module(rsyslogd_tls, 1.0)
require {
  type rsyslogd_t;
  type cert_t;
  class file { read open };
  class tcp_socket { name_bind connectto };
  class net_bind_service;
}
allow rsyslogd_t cert_t:file { read open };
```

```bash
# firewall example
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=6514/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate certificates with minimal log loss?
- How to handle a secondary collector and automatic failover?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests configuring a non-root service, simple Python HTTP server, systemd management, firewall rules, and log rotation in a cohesive, beginner-friendly task. It mirrors real onboarding on production hosts where services run under dedicated users with restricted access.

## Key Concepts
- systemd unit for a non-login user
- Python stdlib HTTPServer handling a specific path
- log rotation configuration
- firewalld port opening and verification
- test plan with curl and log checks

## Code Example
```python
# /home/statapi/status_api.py
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
import json

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path == '/api/status':
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(json.dumps({"status":"ok"}).encode())
        else:
            self.send_error(404)

httpd = HTTPServer(('0.0.0.0', 8080), Handler)
httpd.serve_forever()
```

- How would you containerize this for consistent runtimes across hosts?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to combine systemd scheduling (service + timer), non-root privileges, archiving backups with date suffix, and log rotation for maintainability.

## Key Concepts
- systemd service and timer
- non-login user and file permissions
- tar with date suffix
- logrotate configuration and rotation policies

## Code Example
```bash
# Create non-root user
useradd -r -s /sbin/nologin appback

# Backup script
cat > /usr/local/bin/backup-app.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
tar czf /var/backups/app-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz /home/app >> /var/log/app-backup.log 2>&1
EOF
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/backup-app.sh
chown appback:appback /usr/local/bin/backup-app.sh

# Systemd service
cat > /etc/systemd/system/app-backup.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=App backup script

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=appback
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/backup-app.sh
EOF

# Systemd timer
cat > /etc/systemd/system/app-backup.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Daily app backup timer

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF

# Logrotate
cat > /etc/logrotate.d/app-backup <<'EOF'
/var/log/app-backup.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  compress
  missingok
  notifempty
}
EOF

# Enable and test
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now app-backup.timer
```

## Why This Is Asked

- systemd timer and service pairing
- non-login system users

## Code Example
```bash
# health.sh (as /opt/health/health.sh)
#!/bin/bash
TS=$(date '+%F %T')
OUT="/var/log/health/health.log"
(</dev/tcp/localhost/22) >/dev/null 2>&1; P22=$?
(</dev/tcp/localhost/80) >/dev/null 2>&1; P80=$?
echo "$TS port22=$([ $P22 -eq 0 ] && echo OPEN || echo CLOSED) port80=$([ $P80 -eq 0 ] && echo OPEN || echo CLOSED)" >> "$OUT"
```
```ini
# healthcheck.service
[Unit]
Description=Health check
[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=health
ExecStart=/opt/health/health.sh
```
```ini
# healthcheck.timer
[Unit]
Description=Health check every 5 minutes
[Timer]
OnUnitActiveSec=5min
Unit=healthcheck.service
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```
```text
# /etc/logrotate.d/health
 /var/log/health/health.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  missingok
  notifempty
  compress
  delaycompress
  create 0640 health health
 }
```

- How could you add alerting for frequent failures?
